claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has alternating soft FCC and hard B2 lamellae.
The dual-phase lamellae are organized into a hierarchical colony microstructure.
The untreated eutectic alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent or incoherent internal boundaries create local stress concentrations.
Local stress concentrations cause premature microcracking and brittle or catastrophic failure during straining.
A minor targeted alloying addition during synthesis can induce controlled, uniform coherent nanoprecipitates specifically at lamellar colony interfaces.
Cr is a candidate minor addition for inducing the proposed coherent interfacial nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission across colony boundaries.
The coherent nanoprecipitates improve interfacial connectivity and act as bridges for dislocation motion.
Improved dislocation transmission reduces dislocation pile-ups and associated local stress concentrations.
The nanoprecipitates also provide precipitation strengthening.
The modification will increase elongation to failure while retaining or slightly increasing yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The intervention is expected to be effective under room-temperature tensile loading.
The intervention is expected to be effective at conventional strain rates.
An optimized heat treatment can promote the formation and retention of the proposed coherent interfacial precipitates.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome treats retention of similar strength as success, whereas the falsification rule's 'and/or retains similar or lower strength' wording can treat similar strength as a falsifying result.
